title: The First Mermaid
author: William Saville
content:
I was flung from the ship, my back arching in a final, desperate cry. The icy wind tore at my throat, and my mind burned with the dread of what lay ahead; an unforgiving plunge into the ocean's endless depths, where my grave would be cold, dark, and nameless. When my body hit the water, it was as though I had collided with a wall of ice. Every nerve in my body screamed as the chill sank into my bones. My own scream was cut short, replaced by the searing burn of saltwater flooding my lungs.

I sank, helpless, my limbs flailing weakly against the currents. I couldn’t swim; I had never learned. My thoughts spiraled in panicked regret. I would die here; untouched by love, childless, and forgotten by the world above. I would simply vanish, swallowed by the waves like countless others before me.

The cold tightened its grip, and blackness began to creep into the corners of my vision. My lungs spasmed as they filled completely with water. Death was close, tugging at the edges of my mind, soothing in its finality. I welcomed it. Yet, just as I was about to slip into the void, something stirred.

A voice.

It was distant at first, a whisper tangled in the currents. But it grew louder, resonating in my mind as if the sea itself were speaking.

"Little creature of the earth, how do you find yourself in my waters?"

The words hissed and swirled, cutting through the darkness that had engulfed me. My body remained unresponsive, lifeless, but my mind flickered to life, a faint spark of awareness. I tried to speak, to respond, but my thoughts were jumbled and incoherent.

"You were thrown here? By your own people? Why?"

The voice understood me, even though I could not find the words to explain myself. My thoughts formed a disjointed picture: the abuse I had fled, the desperation that had led me to stow away on a ship, and the cruel fate I had met when discovered.

The voice was silent for a moment, as though considering my story. Then it spoke again, its tone softer but no less commanding.

"You fled pain, yet found none here who would show you mercy. I am no human, but I have more heart than they. If you wish, I will save you. You can live here, with my people, among the waves."

The voice's offer filled me with alarm and wonder. Creatures of the sea? Intelligent life beyond the surface? We had never been taught of such beings. The ocean had always been a place of mystery, a vast expanse ruled by chaos and danger. But I had loved it since I was a child. I would sit at the shoreline, dipping my toes into the surf, dreaming of what lay beyond the horizon. Even as I had boarded that ship in desperation, part of me had been comforted by the thought that, if nothing else, my end would come in the embrace of the sea.

The voice waited patiently, letting me sift through my thoughts without interruption. When I was ready, I reached out with a tentative, wordless "yes."

"It will be done," the voice hissed.

Agony exploded through me, snapping me back into my body. It felt as though hundreds of blades were carving into my flesh, reshaping me. Fire coursed through every vein, yet I could not scream. My body twisted and convulsed, and then, as quickly as it began, the pain was gone.

I opened my eyes.

Raven hair floated around me in the water like a dark halo. My clothes, now too loose, sank into the depths. I was naked, yet I felt no shame; only awe. My legs were gone, replaced by a shimmering tail that ended in a large, elegant fin. Smaller fins flared where my knees had once been. I raised my hands to my face, marveling at the webbing that now stretched between my fingers, and brushed my neck, discovering gills beneath the scales that adorned my once-human skin.

The water around me, once icy and cruel, now felt warm and alive. I could see farther and clearer than I ever had before, my vision unclouded even in the dim light of the deep. Particles of sand and plankton drifted lazily in the currents, catching the light in a way that made the ocean glitter like a sky full of stars.

Before me floated the creature who had saved me. No larger than my fist, it had iridescent scales that shimmered with hues of emerald and sapphire. Its wide, luminous eyes sparkled with intelligence and warmth. It darted around me in playful loops, and I could feel its joy radiating through the bond we now shared.

"Welcome, maiden of the sea," the voice said, though now I could see that it came from the tiny creature itself.

I looked down at my tail, flexing it experimentally. It moved with an effortless grace, propelling me upward with the smallest flick. A laugh bubbled from my throat, surprising me; it sounded musical, like the chime of bells carried on the wind.

I swam, testing my new body, feeling the power in every movement. The sea embraced me, whispering secrets in its endless songs. For the first time in my life, I felt free. I was no longer a creature of the earth, shackled by its pain and limitations.

I was no longer human.

The thought did not terrify me as I had feared. Instead, it filled me with a sense of peace. The sea was my new home, its depths my sanctuary. I could feel the pull of the ocean calling to me, urging me to dive deeper, to explore its vast wonders. Every current was a promise, every wave a new beginning. I was reborn in the sea’s warm embrace, far from the world that had cast me aside.

As I swam, I became aware of the creature beside me; its purpose was clear now. It was my guide, my protector in this strange and beautiful world. And I began to question. I had been given this incredible gift, this new life, but surely there must be others like me; others who had suffered as I had, others who could be saved by the ocean’s embrace.

"Can you find more like me?" I asked the creature. The words slipped from my new, melodic lips, as easy as breathing. "There must be others who are lost, others who need the sea’s mercy."

The creature’s large eyes met mine, full of wisdom and sorrow. "You were cast into the sea for a reason. But those who suffer like you… they are many. Yet the sea does not give freely. It demands sacrifice, and those who come here must earn their place."

I didn’t understand. "What do you mean?"

The creature fluttered around me, its tiny form weaving through the water like a thread of light. "To be made like you; to be saved from the earth’s cruelty; it is not something to be taken lightly. There are those who would seek the sea’s gift for their own gain, who would twist the ocean’s power to their will."

I couldn’t imagine such a thing. The sea had been nothing but kind to me, a sanctuary from the pain of my past. But the creature’s words haunted me.

Weeks passed as I acclimated to my new life beneath the waves. My tail became more graceful, and I learned to navigate the ocean as if I had always belonged there. But my thoughts never strayed far from the idea of bringing more like me into this world. The creature warned me against it, but I could not shake the yearning to rescue others, to create a community of beings who, like me, could find peace in the ocean’s depths.

And so, I petitioned the creature again.

"Please," I implored. "Let me find others. Let me give them what you gave me."

The creature hesitated, then spoke softly. "I will take you to the shores where lost souls wander. There, you may find those who seek what you do. But remember this: the ocean will not give without its price. You will see what becomes of those who seek power without respect for the sea’s laws."

I agreed.

For a time, it was perfect. I brought women; maidens who had suffered at the hands of those who sought to control them; into the sea, offering them a new chance at life. The ocean greeted them with the same warm embrace it had offered me. They were saved, transformed, reborn.

But as the years passed, something shifted. I began to sense a change in those I had brought into the fold. Some grew restless. Some began to demand more; more power, more freedom, more control over the sea. They spoke of creating their own kingdoms beneath the waves, taking what they needed, disregarding the ocean’s delicate balance.

Soon, there were whispers of rebellion. The sea, once a sanctuary, now felt heavy with tension. The creatures who had once been gentle guides began to retreat, and the ocean itself seemed to grow cold.

I had made a mistake. I had created beings like myself, but in doing so, I had awakened something darker; greed, the same thing that had driven me from the land. And now, it threatened to consume the peace we had found beneath the waves.

The ocean was no longer safe. It had become a battlefield, a place where those who had once been saved now sought to dominate. The very creatures I had brought here to heal were now the ones tearing it apart.

In the end, it was clear: the ocean had no place for greed. And neither did I.
